title: Greybox Fuzzing for Concurrency Testing
problem: Finding bugs in concurrent programs is challenging due to the exponentially large search space of thread interleavings. Existing approaches are either optimistic (random sampling) or pessimistic (systematic bounded exploration).
motivation: Detecting bugs in concurrent programs is critical for ensuring software reliability and system correctness.
method: The approach employs biased random search guided by the "reads-from" relation to navigate and prune the thread interleaving search space. It uses reads-from information to identify new behaviors in interleavings and guide exploration toward neighborhoods likely to expose bugs, achieving more uniform schedule space exploration than randomized baselines.
key_novelty: Applying greybox fuzzing principles to concurrency testing by using "reads-from" relations to guide biased random search through thread interleaving space.
contributions: A pragmatic greybox fuzzing approach for concurrency testing that balances formal and unguided testing
Reads-From Fuzzer (RFF) infrastructure for community use and future research
Demonstrated efficiency improvements in bugs found per schedule exercised over state-of-the-art tools
More uniform schedule space exploration compared to randomized baseline scheduling algorithms
